title: ZKC Public Input Binding Classification v1
description: Per-field request-binding classification for a ZKC circuit's public inputs. A sidecar to the immutable public-input encoder document (schemas/public-inputs/<circuit>.json): the encoder freezes the wire shape, this document declares the verifier-side contract for each field. Every public input is classified as 'bound' (the verifier MUST validate it against a value it knows independently of the prover — the leading reference in `source` names where that expected value comes from, and the optional `check` names the comparison kind: 'equals' (the default), 'member_of' an authenticated set, or 'policy_range' against a policy bound; `group` marks fields validated together, such as an (x, y) key pair), 'derived' (the verifier MUST recompute it from the references in `from` and reject on mismatch; the mandatory `note` states the exact recomputation, including any interior hashing of the referenced values — a derived recomputation proves reproducibility, and contributes request binding only through its param:/context:/bound references), or 'free' (the prover chooses it; `justification` records in writing why that is sound). A `param:` reference on a bound field's source, or in a derived field's `from` list, is REQUIRED in the authenticated request: a request lacking it MUST be rejected rather than defaulted, unless the entry's text declares an explicit expectation for that case. Reference vocabulary: 'context:<field>' = authenticated request context, 'param:<camelName>' = authenticated request parameter for this proof type, 'envelope:<path>' = authenticated envelope element (an element the active profile omits resolves to the sentinel the entry's text names), 'policy:<path>' = verifier trust policy or verifier-local authenticated state (including the registry-pinned circuit identity), 'map:predicateTypes[proofType]' = this document's proof-type -> predicate_type map, 'public:<name>' = another public input of the same circuit. Entries are keyed by `name` — consumers MUST bind by name, never by offset (v1/v2 encoders order fields differently). NAME LAYERS: a proof entry's `publicInputs` object is keyed by the snake_case `name` itself; `camelName` is the spelling of the corresponding request parameter and aggregation-envelope keys, MUST equal the mechanical snake_case -> camelCase conversion of `name`, and MUST NOT be used to read a proof entry's `publicInputs`.
